title.narrative: Central African Republic COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Project

description.narrative: The purpose of the COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Project in the Central African Republic is to prepare for and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 (Coronavirus). This project consists of three components. The first component is preparedness and response. This component will finance activities related to activities pertaining to preparedness, case management and response, including procurement of medical equipment and supplies, risk communication and community engagement, including capacity building and coordination. Component two is project implementation. Implementing the proposed project will require monitoring and evidence generation, reporting and impact assessment. Component three is Contingency Emergency Response (CERC). In addition, a CERC will be included for situations of other urgent need of assistance or capacity constraints.
To prepare for and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 in the Central African Republic.

title.narrative: Targeted facilities that have received selected drugs required to respond to the surge in patients due to COVID-19

comment.narrative: All treatment centers (4 in Bangui and 32 in the rest of the country) have received medication by August 2021. The number of treatment centers increased, where in all centers, selected medication to care for the COVID19 patients were supplied:  July 2020:  9 out of 9 health facilities; January 2021:  15 out of 15 health facilities; August 2021:  36 out of 36 health facilities.

title.narrative: Targeted communities informed on hygiene behavior

comment.narrative:
Hygiene promotion activities were organized at the health facility and community levels in the country. Over 250,000 soaps were distributed, in addition to hygiene kits, masks and food stamps, along with hygiene sanitation campaigns with strong community sensitization of COVID19 risk and prevention.Provision and treatment of potable water was also realized in 10 districts in the country. 
As this activity will  continue under the AF, the end target date will be extended.

title.narrative: Personal protective equipment (PPE) kit (masks, face shield, gloves, gown) delivered to targeted health facilities

comment.narrative: Exceeded end target under the original financing phase by almost two-fold. This indicator is no longer tracked under the AF.

title.narrative: COVID-19 risk communication messages broadcasted to communities (number of days)

comment.narrative: Mobile COVID-19 voice messages began being transmitted on April 27, 2020, and has been active since then. The support is no longer continued under the AF phase.

title.narrative: Health staff trained in infection prevention per MOH-approved protocols

comment.narrative: Exceeded end target for original financing phase. This indicator is no longer tracked during AF phase.

title.narrative: Additional patient "beds" made available in designated care centers and hospitals

comment.narrative: Exceeded end target under the original financing phase. This activity is no longer supported under AF phase and indicator no longer tracked.

title.narrative: Laboratories with trained staff and consumables for collecting COVID-19 samples and transporting to Pasteur Institute laboratory (IBP)

comment.narrative: Initial target was set at 15 assuming only district hospital laboratories. However, a large number of primary level health facilities staff in CAR where they have small laboratories were also trained and are now also collecting COVID-19 samples. The actuals include these facilities.  The indicator is no longer tracked under the AF.

title.narrative: Risk comminication strategy developed and disseminated

comment.narrative: Strategy has been elaborated and the govt is starting to use it in parts.

title.narrative: M&E system established to monitor COVID-19 preparedness and response

comment.narrative: Surveillance data on COVID19 cases are collected and reports are disseminated through the Emergency response committee (COUSP) of the Ministry of Health and WHO.  So a surveillance system is operating (which started before Project effectiveness), but this is the surveillance of COVID-19 itself, and not a more comprehensive Monitoring & Evaluation of overall preparednessnd response.  There are two initiatives underway to put in place systems for disease surveillance overall, which are not yet completed.
